correctness.rationale: A complete antipodal transversal gives a positive integer cyclic gap vector of length n and total 2n. Discrete strict-concavity unit transfers prove the majorization inequality with equality only at equal gap multisets. The concentrated (n+1,1,...,1) vector dominates every candidate, yielding exactly the consecutive minimizers. The balanced all-2 vector is attainable only for odd n. For even n, integrality forces every nonuniform gap vector to majorize (3,2,...,2,1); the required even/odd count in antipodal pairs fixes the gap 1 and gap 3 half a cycle apart. These patterns are realized, so all inequalities are sharp and the strictness classification complete. The chord perimeter follows by substitution, trigonometric identity and Taylor expansion. The package has a standalone exhaustive small-order regression program.
risks: The finite checker is used solely for regression, not infinite certification.
Strict concavity, even parity, all equality cases, and positivity of gaps are essential assumptions.

originality.rationale: Full primary work arXiv:1301.6667v1 solves area extrema and explicitly proposes perimeter as a separate natural extremal measure in Section 6. The 2015 follow-up arXiv:1501.07721v1 analyzes maximum area for fewer selected pairs. Their exact area-pattern statements do not give sharp perimeter values nor a theorem for all strictly concave edge-gap energies. A constrained lattice majorization argument supplies a complete quantitative answer, including a parity penalty and all equality classes. Targeted semantic database searches under geometric and musical aliases returned no implication-equivalent statement.

value.rationale: The motivating antipodal-polygon source explicitly proposes perimeter as a meaningful alternative to the solved area problem. The theorem resolves that natural full-transversal regular-lattice problem for all n with unique strict equality classes and sharp explicit perimeter values. A strictly concave gap-energy majorization theorem unifies the family and explains the parity obstruction and exact cubic asymptotic perimeter loss. These are not merely area facts or arbitrary numerical slices.
risks: The result is restricted to regular circular lattices; arbitrary antipodal point configurations remain unsolved for perimeter.
